newsitem.title: USA: Conservatives slam Weld for attack on Republicans.
newsitem.headline: Conservatives slam Weld for attack on Republicans.

text.p: U.S. conservatives on Saturday questioned whether William Weld deserved a hearing on his nomination as ambassador to Mexico, saying the former Massachusetts governor had insulted Sen. Jesse Helms.

They said Weld had "kicked sand in the face of the Senate" by facing down Helms, the North Carolina chairman of the powerful Senate Foreign Relations Committee, and Weld should apologise to Helms if he wants to get a hearing.
Weld, a Republican moderate, has drawn fire from his conservative colleagues by taking on their icon and accusing Helms of "ideological extortion" in opposing his nomination.
Helms has refused to hold a nomination hearing for Weld, who resigned as governor of Massachusetts on Tuesday midway through his second term to fight for the diplomatic post.
The two men are at opposite poles of the Republican Party, with Helms embracing its traditional conservative policies and Weld firmly committed to progressive ideals.

Sen. Chuck Hagel, a Nebraska Republican on the foreign relations committee, said a completely "bizarre" set of circumstances had developed since Democratic President Bill Clinton chose Weld to be U.S. ambassador to Mexico.

"Diplomats should be engaged in stopping wars not beginning wars ... you just don't go around doing the things he's done and saying the things he said and thinking that the Senate or the chairman is going to open up a hearing automatically," Hagel said on CNN's Inside Politics Weekend.

Helms charges that Weld is "soft" on drugs and hence unsuitable for the post in Mexico, a major transit route for narcotics reaching the United States. He has also said he does not think Weld is "ambassador quality."
Republican conservatives also questioned Weld's ability to do the job and said he should apologise to Helms.

"This guy's goofy. He's quit every job he's had. He might not like the water in Mexico if you confirm him, and leave the second week after he's there," David Keene, president of the American Conservative Union, who has vowed to lead the fight against Weld's nomination, said on the same CNN programme.
Weld made the customary round of Washington stops this week for a prospective ambassador, meeting White House staff, paying courtesy calls on senators and receiving briefings at the State Department.
"A fair hearing is all I'm looking for," he said. "I call on Sen. Helms to explain why there shouldn't be a fair hearing."
